puzzles.title: The Locked Safe
puzzles.room_description: You're in a dimly lit server room. Cables snake across the floor. A heavy safe sits against the wall. On the wall hangs a faded chart.

safe.description: A heavy iron safe with a keypad. Binary sequences are etched into the door.
safe.examine:
Two sequences are engraved: [ 01001000 ] [ 01001001 ]
The keypad has a prompt: 'Enter the ASCII characters.'

chart.description: A faded poster on the wall.
chart.examine:
An ASCII reference chart. Useful values:
  H = 72 = 01001000
  I = 73 = 01001001
  A = 65  B = 66  C = 67 ...

keypad.description: A numeric keypad beside the safe.
keypad.examine: The keypad accepts text input. Type your answer to unlock the safe.

hints: There's an ASCII chart on the wall - try EXAMINE CHART.
Convert each group of 8 bits to a decimal number first.

puzzles.title: The Cipher Machine
puzzles.room_description: A dusty room with an old mechanical cipher machine humming on the table. A note is pinned to the wall beside it.

machine.description: An old cipher machine with a screen and a rotating dial.
machine.examine:
The screen reads: KHOOR ZRUOG
The dial is set to 3.
A label reads: 'Shift back to reveal the truth.'

note.description: A note pinned to the wall.
note.examine:
The note reads:
'Each letter has been shifted forward in the alphabet.
To decode, use: DECODE <message> <shift>'
Example: DECODE KHOOR ZRUOG 3

hints: Each letter has been moved forward in the alphabet by the number on the dial.
To decode, move each letter back by 3 positions. K becomes H, H becomes E, etc.
Try typing: DECODE KHOOR ZRUOG 3

puzzles.title: The Combination Cabinet
puzzles.room_description: A tall cabinet sealed with three combination locks. A screen above each lock displays a sequence of numbers with the last one missing.

rounds.explanation: Powers of 2 - each number is doubled.
Fibonacci sequence - each number is the sum of the two before it.
Triangular numbers - the gap between each number increases by 1 each time.

cabinet.description: A tall cabinet with three combination locks.
cabinet.examine:
Lock 1: [LOCKED]  Lock 2: [LOCKED]  Lock 3: [LOCKED]
Each lock has a sequence of numbers displayed above it.
You must find the next number in each sequence to unlock it.

screen.description: A screen above the cabinet showing the current sequence.
screen.examine:
The screen shows a sequence of numbers ending with a question mark.
Type ENTER <number> to submit your answer.

hints: Look at the relationship between consecutive numbers in the sequence.
Are the numbers being added together, multiplied, or something else?
Round 1: try doubling the last number.

puzzles.title: The Logic Gate Lock
puzzles.room_description: You face a large, heavy door with 4 coloured switches: A,B,C and D, and a display showing a Boolean expression.

door.description: A heavy door with four switches and a display above it.
door.examine:
The display reads: (A AND B) OR (NOT C)
The light above the door is RED. [LOCKED]

switches.description: Four coloured switches labelled A, B, C and D.
switches.examine:
Each switch can be ON (1) or OFF (0).
Use FLIP <switch> to toggle a switch.
Example: FLIP A

manual.description: A laminated instruction card on the wall.
manual.examine:
Boolean logic reference:
  AND - true only if BOTH sides are true
  OR  - true if EITHER side is true
  NOT - inverts the value (0 becomes 1, 1 becomes 0)

hints: Try EXAMINE MANUAL to read the logic reference card.
Work from the inside out. What makes (NOT C) true?
If C is 0, then NOT C is 1. OR only needs one side to be true - so the whole expression becomes true.

puzzles.title: The Maze of Nodes
puzzles.room_description: You enter a dark network of tunnels. An ASCII map is pinned to the wall showing rooms connected by passages. Somewhere ahead is the exit.

map.description: A hand-drawn map of the tunnel network pinned to the wall.

sign.description: A worn sign near the entrance.
sign.examine:
The sign reads:
  Each room is connected to others by tunnels.
  You can only move to rooms directly connected to your current room.
  Use MOVE <node> to travel.
  Use LOOK to see your current connections.
  Use PATH to review where you have been.
  Use BACK to retrace your last step.

hints: Try EXAMINE MAP to see the tunnel layout.
From A, you can go to B or D. Think about which direction gets you closer to X.
The shortest path visits 4 nodes. Try exploring level by level rather than going deep in one direction.
Shortest path: A -> B -> C -> X

puzzles.title: The Corrupted File
puzzles.room_description: A terminal displays a corrupted data grid. Parity bits line the edges.

terminal.description: A glowing terminal showing binary data.
terminal.examine: Rows and columns use EVEN parity. One bit is incorrect.

hints: Even parity means even number of 1s
Check rows and columns
Find where both fail

puzzles.title: The Robot Navigator
puzzles.room_description: A small robot sits in a grid-based room filled with obstacles. You must program it to reach the exit.

grid.description: A grid showing the robot, walls, and exit.
grid.examine:
> = Robot (facing right at start)  X = Exit  # = Wall
Valid commands: MOVE, TURN LEFT, TURN RIGHT
Submit with: PROGRAM MOVE, TURN RIGHT, MOVE, ...

hints: Plan your full route before running - commands execute all at once and you can't adjust mid-run.
Use TURN LEFT and TURN RIGHT to change direction, then MOVE to advance one square.
Try heading right one step, then turning south and working your way down and around to the bottom-right exit.

puzzles.title: The Scrambled Bookshelf
puzzles.room_description: A tall bookshelf blocks a hidden doorway. Books are numbered but in the wrong order. A bronze plaque reads: 'Arrange me using the method of bubbles, and the door shall open.'

bookshelf.description: A tall bookshelf blocking a hidden doorway. Books are numbered and out of order.
bookshelf.examine:
Six numbered books sit on the shelf: [8] [3] [5] [1] [9] [2]
A plaque reads: 'Arrange me using the method of bubbles, and the door shall open.'
Use SWAP <n> <m> to swap two neighbouring books.

plaque.description: A bronze plaque fixed to the shelf.
plaque.examine:
The plaque reads:
'Arrange me using the method of bubbles, and the door shall open.
Swap only neighbouring books. The largest number will bubble to the end.'

hints: Bubble sort works by repeatedly swapping adjacent elements that are in the wrong order.
Start from the left - compare books 1 and 2. If book 1 is larger, swap them, then move to books 2 and 3.
The largest number will 'bubble' to the right end after one full pass. Optimal solution takes 9 swaps.

puzzles.title: The Stack Overflow — Data Structure Challenge
puzzles.room_description: Two conveyor belts sit side by side: one behaves like a stack (LIFO) and the other like a queue (FIFO). Crates labelled A–F arrive in a fixed order. You must use PUSH, POP, ENQUEUE, and DEQUEUE to produce the target output.

stack.description: A vertical conveyor belt that behaves like a stack.
stack.examine: The stack takes items with PUSH and returns the most recent item with POP.

queue.description: A horizontal conveyor belt that behaves like a queue.
queue.examine: The queue takes items with ENQUEUE and returns the oldest item with DEQUEUE.

input_belt.description: A belt delivering crates in a fixed order.
input_belt.examine: Crates arrive labelled A through F. You must decide where each crate goes.

output_shelf.description: A shelf where crates must be placed in the correct target order.
output_shelf.examine: The target order is displayed beside the shelf.

hints: Stacks return the most recent item (LIFO).
Queues return the oldest item (FIFO).
Use the stack to reverse short sequences.
Use the queue to preserve order when needed.
Plan ahead — once a crate is placed on the output shelf, it cannot be moved.

puzzles.title: The Final Exit Door
puzzles.room_description: A heavy steel door blocks your escape. A keypad awaits a number between 1 and 100.

door.description: A reinforced exit door with a glowing keypad.
door.examine: The door has no handle—only a keypad and a small display screen. A note reads: 'Seven guesses. Higher or lower.'

keypad.description: A numeric keypad with worn-out buttons.
keypad.examine: You can type GUESS [number]. The display will tell you if the secret number is TOO HIGH or TOO LOW.

screen.description: A small digital display above the keypad.
screen.examine: The screen flashes: 'Enter a number between 1 and 100. Attempts remaining: 7.'

hints: Binary search is the only guaranteed method to solve this in 7 guesses.
Start by guessing the midpoint of the range.
Each response eliminates half of the remaining numbers.
log2(100) is about 7, meaning you can always find the number if you halve the range each time.
